text:
maria: Heads-up — for the last hour we're seeing a rising Pending backlog on eu-west1 GPU nodes. ~40 pods stuck, though cluster has ostensibly free GPU capacity.
lee: any evictions/restarts?
maria: Not many evictions. kube-scheduler is placing, but pods never bind to nodes. Node pools show 1 GPU free on many nodes. Suspect fencepost allocation: pods request fractional/1-gpu and get spread.
sam: Are those pods using `nvidia.com/gpu: 1` or device-plugin counts?
maria: `nvidia.com/gpu: 1`. A lot are short-lived fine-grain jobs from our eval fleet. They tend to avoid packing because of podAntiAffinity we added last quarter.
lee: ugh that affinity + daemonsets + gpu shard sizing = fragmentation. Can you paste `kubectl get nodes -o custom-columns=NODE:.metadata.name,GPU:.allocatable`?
maria: quick dump:
```
node-gpu-eu-1   8
node-gpu-eu-2   7
node-gpu-eu-3   1
node-gpu-eu-4   1
node-gpu-eu-5   8
...
```
We have a lot of 1-GPU remainder nodes. Scheduler leaves single-GPU slots spread across AZs. Jobs require gang/colocated cache locality.
devon: Is the descheduler running? We used to run a nightly compact job but turned it off for stability.
maria: descheduler is currently disabled in eu-west1 for fear of churn after last incident.
arjun: If descheduler is off, small jobs will fragment. Two levers: (1) enable periodic compacting (2) admission control to prefer packing onto nodes with >1 free GPU. Also consider node-size mix — more 4x GPUs and fewer 1x leftovers.
tina: Cost note — increasing large-node count reduces number of partially used nodes and lowers unit cost, but it raises preemption risk for spot. We trade off committed vs spot pools.
sam: Could we change podAffinity/AntiAffinity rules for the eval fleet? They don't need cross-az anti-affinity, only cross-node. That would allow tighter binpacking.
maria: Good call. They're using `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` but with topologies set to zone, so it spreads across AZs. We can change to node or remove.
lee: Quick mitigation: enable a short descheduler pass every 15m with conservative threshold (only move pods when node has <20% CPU or <10% GPU used). Put it behind a feature flag for eu-west1.
arjun: Also consider admission-controller mutation: if request is `nvidia.com/gpu: 1` and there exists a node with >=2 contiguous free GPUs in same AZ, set `preferredScheduling` to favor that node. 
devon: That mutating logic is heavy but doable. We can prototype with a scheduler extender that scores nodes by contiguous free GPUs.
tina: Ops question — will autoprovisioning scale up more 1-gpu nodes if we try to pack? We must ensure cluster-autoscaler profiles favor mid-size instances.
maria: current autoscaler profile is default; it often picks smallest GPU SKU for quicker scaleups, which actually makes fragmentation worse.
sam: Proposed short-term plan: 1) patch eval CI to relax AZ anti-affinity (owner: sam) 2) re-enable conservative descheduler in eu-west1 behind FF (owner: devon) 3) change autoscaler preferred-instance-size to favor 4-GPU SKUs for eu-west1 (owner: tina) 4) spike an internal scheduler-extender prototype for contiguous-GPU scoring (owner: arjun).
lee: +1. Can we also schedule a 2hr maintenance window to test descheduler so we can watch rollback? Put monitoring on PodPending and orphaned GPU counts.
maria: I'll open a runbook and add grafana panel thresholds. ops-bot: Incident note — created ticket INF-8723 for "eu-west1 GPU fragmentation spike" and scheduled review at 10:30 UTC.
arjun: One more thought — KV cache locality: some model-serving pods require the same NVCache locality; moving them might increase cold-cache misses. Descheduler should skip pods labeled `no-evict-cache`.
devon: Good point. We'll add label skip to critical cache-sensitive workloads.
tina: Also run a cost sim after changes; doubling 4-GPU nodes might change committed vs spot ratio.
sam: I'll relax the affinity and run a small canary at 11:00 UTC.
maria: Thanks all — will push the FF for descheduler and update the ticket with smoke results. :thumbsup:
lee: Thanks. Keep thread updated.
